messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service: edge-lb-health (severity: P1) — symptoms: spike in TLS handshake failures and 502s from the edge LB. Paging on-call.

pagerduty: Incident created — incident id: PD-45231. Escalation policy: infra-oncall -> infra-lead.

maria: saw a sudden jump in errors ~2m ago. Grafana: client TLS errors (0x14094410) up from ~3/min to ~120/min. 502s from gateway spiking. Not all regions affected. EU-edge primarily.

devon: acked. I’m oncall, joining. Quick ask: are we seeing unhealthy targets or TLS negotiation failures at the ALB?

sanjay: checking target group health now. running: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:tg:eu-west-1:...`

sanjay: output: UnhealthyCount=3/12 for tg-edge-eu. Reason: TLS handshake timeout from node t-az2-03.

olivia: seeing DNS TTLs still 60s for edge custom domain -> route53 records look fine. No mass change recently.

maria: correlation: client TLS errors map to requests routed to t-az2-03. That host has high CPU and kernel logs show `SSL_read: connection reset by peer`.

devon: can we drain and remove t-az2-03? If it’s a bad instance, fail it out of target group to stop TLS resets.

ursula: PagerDuty note: devon is responding. Escalation paused.

sanjay: initiating: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg:eu-west-1:... --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d` (i-0a1b2c3d = t-az2-03).

olivia: reweighting traffic: switching weighted routing for eu-edge from 100% primary -> 0% primary, 100% fallback via regional failover (short cold-path) — doing via route53 weights.

maria: rolling. note: clients with long-lived connections may keep failing until TLS renegotiation. amplitude shows increased retries for a handful of large customers.

devon: removed i-0a1b2c3d from TG. wait for healthy count to return.

sanjay: new target health: UnhealthyCount=0/11 after deregister, inflight connections dropping. LB metrics: 502 rate falling back to baseline in last 60s.

maria: verifying TLS handshake histogram — p50 latency restored, p99 still slightly elevated (due to retries).

olivia: DNS failover completed, new weights propagated (Route53 change id: Z123456789). TTL is 60s; will normalize in ~60s for all clients.

maria: customer impact: observed elevated error rates for 3 enterprise customers (cust-A, cust-B, cust-C) in EU region for ~4m. We should notify CS for those accounts.

devon: notifying CS: @cs-team please alert cust-A/B/C that we experienced transient edge TLS failures in EU; mitigation applied (instance removed + regional weight shift). ETA to fully recover for some clients: up to 2m for client-side DNS/connection churn.

pagerduty: Acknowledgement recorded by devon at 2871230025.

incident-bot: auto-log: runbook step 'remove-unhealthy-target' executed by sanjay.

maria: I’m collecting logs from t-az2-03 for a postmortem: suspected library-level SSL bug (OpenSSL 1.1.1 patch level mismatch).

olivia: Can you confirm if there's been a recent AMI or package rollout on that hostgroup?

sanjay: checking deploy history: there was an automated security patch on that hostgroup yesterday (~03:00 UTC) that touched openssl libs. Rolling back just for that host might be noisy.

devon: short-term mitigation applied. Next steps: pin rollout, roll rest of TG hosts through to confirm no wider impact. Ops: schedule controlled reboot and force HTTPS handshake test on remaining instances.

maria: running smoke: `openssl s_client -connect t-az2-01:443 -servername edge.example.com` shows successful handshake. `t-az2-03` log has `unexpected eof while reading`.

olivia: customer-facing note drafted: "We experienced a short-lived edge TLS handshake error affecting EU region. We have rerouted traffic and removed the impacted instance. Some customers may have seen transient errors; monitoring continues." Please sign-off devon/maria.

devon: sign-off. olivia, go ahead and post to #customer-impact with that note and reference incident id PD-45231.

maria: adding config diff to ticket: candidate fix = revert openssl package on host image and re-run healthcheck. Also add canary with 10% traffic before broad rollout.

sanjay: ticketing: created internal issue INFRA-7823 with logs + commands + host image id.

devon: handoff: I need to hand this to infra-backfill in 20m. Oncall secondary = ursula, please be ready to take post incident follow-ups.

ursula: acked, will watch metrics and PD for the next 30m.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation suppressed (acknowledged by oncall). Auto-close policy: will notify if error rate > 5x baseline again.

maria: current status: mitigation applied, client error rate down to ~1.2x baseline, key customers flagged, CS notified. Postmortem owner: sanjay.

olivia: final note: we should check our image rollout windows and add an alert on openssl library upgrades to catch regression earlier.

devon: agreed. filing follow-up action items and will close incident when metrics stable for 30 more minutes.

maria: thanks team. I’ll gather timeline and hand to sanjay for postmortem.

sanjay: timeline captured in INFRA-7823, will kick off RCA tomorrow and include remediation plan (pin image, controlled canary, add TLS handshake monitoring).

incident-bot: Incident PD-45231 set to status: monitoring.

pagerduty: Incident PD-45231: last update recorded at 2871230360.

maria: closing thread here, will update the ticket with any late regressions.
